subject: Geopolitics
title: Iraq WMD Debacle
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Iraq WMD Debacle.

hook.text: The US invaded Iraq in 2003 over weapons of mass destruction. They didn't exist. Intelligence was wrong.

buildup.text: Analysts were pressured to confirm what leaders already believed. 'Curveball,' a key source, was fabricating data.

discovery.text: Groupthink took over. Dissenting voices were sidelined. The intelligence community told leaders what they wanted.

twist.text: The failure wasn't just analytical — it was political.

climax.text: The Iraq WMD disaster destroyed intelligence credibility for a generation. Now even valid warnings are doubted.

punchline.text: When intelligence serves politics, truth is the first casualty.

quiz.question: What role did groupthink play in the Iraq WMD failure?
options: Analysts unanimously agreed WMDs existed based on evidence
Dissenting voices were sidelined and leaders heard what they wanted
Groupthink led to overestimating Iraq's military strength
